SummerAuthorityAnalytics.name: SummerAuthorityAnalytics
SummerAuthorityAnalytics.brief: Captures creator events through the private Supervisor.
SummerAuthorityAnalytics.description: Use [code]Summer.authority.analytics.capture("wave_completed", {"wave": 3})[/code] from a hosted authority. The Supervisor supplies the current Game, Build, World and runtime identity after checking its active lease. Events describe the authority runtime, not an individual player or an inferred Match. These are creator observations, distinct from reserved platform facts. No route, scope or credential is exposed to game code. Local emulators and older Supervisors do not provide analytics persistence.

methods.name: capture
methods.description: Returns immediately and succeeds only after durable persistence or a persisted duplicate acknowledgment. Properties must be bounded JSON values; reserved platform event names cannot be emitted. At most 32 captures are pending. Submissions use a separate bounded transport lane so analytics cannot block admission or lifecycle traffic. A single attempt uses a 25-second deadline including queue time. Every public failure is nonretryable; an uncertain acknowledgment may already have persisted, and calling capture again creates a new event. An older Supervisor reports [code]not_configured[/code]; quota denial reports [code]analytics_storage_limit_exceeded[/code]. Closing the World cancels pending operations. Process exit may lose pending observations. Never make gameplay depend on analytics delivery.

SummerAuthorityMatch.name: SummerAuthorityMatch
SummerAuthorityMatch.description: Authority-only facade for Match settlement and lifecycle operations. It resolves the trusted World binding internally; game code supplies immutable [SummerSession] capabilities and never peer IDs, supervisor routes, credentials, or runtime-role checks.

methods.name: complete_delivery
methods.description: Finalizes the current persistent or multi-Match delivery phase after every required delivery plan is terminal. Match-bound Sessions end, World-bound Sessions remain admitted, and the World returns to serving. Match-scoped Worlds use [method SummerAuthorityWorld.complete].

methods.name: conclude
methods.description:
Commits one exact outcome for every trusted outcome-eligible participant and returns the typed durable settlement. Spectators, ineligible participants, raw identifiers, forged same-ID Sessions, and divergent retries are rejected.
[param rating_deltas] reports the game's own rating movement for each player, within ±1000, on a queue declared with [code]"ratingSystemRef": "authority_v1"[/code]; see [SummerAuthorityRatings]. Such a queue requires a delta for every participant, and every other queue rejects any delta: the platform refuses the result with [code]invalid_request[/code] and nothing is committed, so the authority may conclude again with corrected arguments. Keys must be Sessions named in [param outcomes].
On a queue that declares teams, the platform scores the sides matchmaking formed from each player's [member SummerParticipant.team]; the outcomes name players, never teams. Give every member of one team the same outcome.

SummerAuthorityPlayerData.name: SummerAuthorityPlayerData
SummerAuthorityPlayerData.description:
Remembers things about a player between play sessions: progress, unlocks, settings. Each player has two separately written slots for this Game: [code]public[/code], which the player's own client can read through [member SummerClient.player_data], and [code]secret[/code], which only the authority reads. Nothing here is visible to other players.
Each slot holds one JSON object of at most 64 KiB. Supported values are [bool], [int] (within ±(2^53 - 1)), finite [float], [String], [Array] and [Dictionary] with [String] keys, nested at most 16 containers deep; anything else fails with [code]player_data_unsupported_type[/code] before a request is sent. Loaded numbers come back as [int] when integral.
Only the player's newest Session for this Game can commit. A commit made through an older Session fails with [code]player_data_superseded[/code]. Commits remain available after gameplay quiesces for shutdown, until the World's stop deadline.
[codeblock]
var player_data := Summer.authority.player_data
var loaded := player_data.load(session)
await loaded.get_result_or_completed_signal()
var progress: Dictionary = loaded.public_record.data
var saved := player_data.commit_public(session, "rift-%d" % run, {"keystone": 7})
var result: SummerResult = await saved.get_result_or_completed_signal()
[/codeblock]

methods.name: commit_public
methods.description: Replaces the player's public slot with [param data]. [param save_id] names this save: resending the same [param save_id] with the same content returns the original revision with [member SummerPlayerDataCommitOperation.replayed] set, while different content fails with [code]player_data_save_id_conflict[/code]. One commit per Session and slot may be pending; another fails with [code]operation_in_progress[/code]. The Engine never retries; on a retryable failure, commit again with the same [param save_id].

methods.name: commit_secret
methods.description: Replaces the player's secret slot with [param data]. It follows the same rules as [method commit_public], and the player's client can never read it.

methods.name: load
methods.description: Reads both slots for the player of [param session]. A slot that was never written has [member SummerPlayerDataRecord.exists] set to [code]false[/code] and an empty [member SummerPlayerDataRecord.data].

SummerAuthorityRankings.name: SummerAuthorityRankings
SummerAuthorityRankings.brief: Trusted reads and versioned writes for Game-scoped rankings.
SummerAuthorityRankings.description: The current World authority can read and compare-and-set a score by stable player ID without a matchmaking Session. A write uses the version returned by [method get_score]. On a version conflict, read and recompute. After a transport failure, read to determine whether the write committed before making another decision. Game code never handles the Supervisor credential.

methods.name: get_score
methods.description: Reads one player's score. The operation carries [member SummerRankingOperation.rating] with value, games and version.

methods.name: leaderboard
methods.description: Reads the ranking's public top 50 rows. No row is marked as the authority's player.

methods.name: set_score
methods.description: Compares [param expected_version] and sets the absolute [param value] and [param games] atomically. A missing score has version zero. Values are bounded to ±1000000000000, games to 2147483647, and versions to safe integers. The expected version must be below 9007199254740991 so the next version remains representable. The Engine does not automatically retry a write.

SummerAuthorityRatings.name: SummerAuthorityRatings
SummerAuthorityRatings.brief: Authority read of each player's queue rating.

methods.name: leaderboard
methods.description: Reads [param queue]'s 50 highest-rated players, the same list every player of the Game can read, with no row marked as the caller. Use it for in-World displays such as a trophy wall in a hub. One read is in flight at a time: a second call for the same queue returns the pending operation, and a call for another queue fails with [code]operation_in_progress[/code]. Fails with [code]rating_unavailable[/code] for a queue that keeps no rating and [code]queue_not_found[/code] for one the active Build does not declare.

methods.name: load
methods.description: Reads the current rating of the player behind [param session] in the queue that admitted it. A second call for the same Session while the first is pending returns the same operation. Fails with [code]rating_unavailable[/code] when that queue keeps no rating and [code]session_not_found[/code] when the platform does not place the Session in this World. The Engine never retries; on a retryable failure, call again.

SummerAuthorityWorld.name: SummerAuthorityWorld
SummerAuthorityWorld.description: Authority-only facade for explicit World lifecycle operations. Completing a World is separate from committing a Match settlement so required post-Match projections have a bounded delivery phase.

methods.name: get_shutdown_notice
methods.description: Current platform maintenance notice, or [code]null[/code]. Connect [signal shutdown_notice_changed], then read this getter to include a notice received before subscription. Cancellation returns [code]null[/code]; stale reordered notices never restore cancelled state.

methods.name: complete
methods.description: Idempotently ends a Match-scoped or persistent World after settlement and required delivery have reached a terminal state. A persistent World must first finish restoring its selected save. Completion permanently ends the logical World; it is not a request to sleep or save it. Multi-Match Worlds use [method SummerAuthorityMatch.complete_delivery] instead.

methods.name: load_save
methods.description: Load and integrity-check the current World save. Existing schema and Build must be compatible. Before initial restore completes, admission remains closed.

methods.name: commit_save
methods.description: Commit an internally consistent game capture after restore. Data is bounded to 16 MiB. Revision and state sequence are canonical nonnegative int64 decimal strings. Save identity and schema are bounded to 128 UTF-8 bytes. Retrying must retain all arguments exactly; conflicting identity reuse or base revision is rejected. The game defines serialization and coupled inventory consistency.

methods.name: finish_restore
methods.description: Call only after applying and validating the successful load result. Admission opens only after the World owner confirms this exact runtime and revision. A foreign, stale or failed load cannot authorize readiness.

methods.name: finish_snapshot
methods.description: Acknowledge a platform save request using a committed receipt. The owner verifies that the save was produced by this runtime after the request. This does not complete or delete the logical World. A successful final acknowledgment may stop this runtime before its completion signal reaches game code; do not rely on code after awaiting it.

methods.name: get_snapshot_request_id
methods.description: Current platform save request, or empty. Query after connecting [signal save_requested] so requests delivered earlier are not missed.

methods.name: get_snapshot_deadline_unix_msec
methods.description: Current platform save deadline in Unix milliseconds, or zero.

signals.name: shutdown_notice_changed
signals.description: The platform announces, revises, or cancels maintenance. A [code]null[/code] notice means cancellation before final saving begins. During advance notice, finish game events or persist their phase. At the preparation boundary, native gameplay input and simulation stop; [signal save_requested] and save operation completions continue. Serialize directly in that callback and use [method commit_save] followed by [method finish_snapshot]. Do not wait for a scene frame, timer, or unrelated deferred callback during final saving. The stop deadline remains binding if the game does not acknowledge. A restart restores the same logical World; it never implies a gameplay wipe or a promise that replacement is already ready.

signals.name: save_requested
signals.description: The platform requests a coherent final save before its deadline. Commit first, then acknowledge using [method finish_snapshot]. Process crashes cannot deliver this signal, so periodic saves are still required.

SummerClient.name: SummerClient
SummerClient.description: This root exists only for a client execution context. Its identity remains stable while immutable context projections advance after admission or reconnect; authority operations are never attached.

methods.name: join
leave
methods.description:
Leaves the current World, or abandons a join still in flight, and clears the client transport.
During hosted matchmaking, await the returned operation before exiting the client. Success means the Player Host acknowledged cancellation or reported that the ticket was already terminal, including when ticket creation was still in flight. A Host failure or request deadline returns a failure; it does not prove the ticket was cancelled. Repeated calls share the pending leave and preserve its result until another join starts.
Leaving an established hosted World closes its local connection promptly, then succeeds only when the Player Host confirms removal of the exact Session through its authenticated completion event or a bounded recovery read. If proof is still unknown at the leave deadline, the result is retryable and retains that Session identity for retry. A local fixture World only clears its local connection. Calling [method SummerOperation.cancel] on a join only cancels that local operation; use [method leave] to await hosted cleanup.

The Host supplies the private player, game, build and analytics-session identity. No URL or credential is available to game code. An authenticated Host advertising analytics support is required.

methods.name: capture
methods.description: Returns immediately. Completion succeeds after durable persistence (including an already-persisted retry). Properties must be JSON values; platform naming and property policies apply, and reserved platform event names cannot be emitted. At most 32 submissions are pending; excess calls fail with [code]capacity_exceeded[/code]. A platform storage-quota rejection reports [code]analytics_storage_limit_exceeded[/code] with retryable false. Capture results never recommend automatic recapture. One submission is made within the service deadline; automatic retries are disabled. An unavailable or timed-out result may already have persisted. Calling capture again creates a new event, so do not recapture the same action to recover an uncertain acknowledgment. Process exit may lose pending observations. Never make gameplay depend on analytics delivery.

methods.description: Reads the player's permissions and, while access is granted, their friends again. Normally unnecessary. One read is in flight at a time; a second call while pending returns the same operation. Succeeds when the friends were read. Fails with [code]permission_not_requested[/code], [code]permission_declined[/code], [code]permission_revoked[/code] or [code]permission_undeclared[/code] when the player has not granted access (the view is then empty), [code]capability_unavailable[/code] when [method is_available] is [code]false[/code] for lack of the capability, [code]age_restricted[/code], [code]unavailable[/code] (retryable) when the Player Host cannot be reached, or [code]protocol_error[/code] for a malformed read, which changes nothing.

methods.name: request_access
methods.description: Asks the Summer app to show its consent sheet for [code]social.friends.read[/code]. Only the trusted app records the player's decision; the Engine then reads it, and the operation completes with it: success once the player granted access, after [signal access_changed] and [signal changed] have fired, or [code]permission_declined[/code] or [code]permission_not_requested[/code] (the player closed the sheet without deciding). It succeeds at once when access is already granted, fails at once with [code]permission_undeclared[/code] when this Build does not declare the permission, and fails with [code]ui_unavailable[/code] when the app cannot show the sheet now. One consent sheet is requested at a time; while it is pending, a second call returns the same operation.

methods.name: show_chat
methods.description: Asks the Summer app to open its direct-message thread with the friend [param user_id] over the game. Completes when the app's presenter answers, as soon as the screen is shown; fails with [code]ui_unavailable[/code] when the app cannot show it now, [code]invalid_argument[/code] for a malformed ID or this player's own, and [code]capability_unavailable[/code] when the Summer app offers no friends or parties. The overlays share the party sheets' presenter: one request is in flight at a time, the same request while pending returns the same operation, and any other fails with retryable [code]operation_in_progress[/code].

methods.name: show_friends
methods.description: Asks the Summer app to show its friends list over the game. Needs no consent. Completion and failures match [method show_chat].

methods.name: show_profile
methods.description: Asks the Summer app to show the profile of the player [param user_id] over the game, with its add-friend, message, invite-to-party and report actions. [param user_id] can be any other player this Game knows, such as a [SummerParticipant] in the current match. Completion and failures match [method show_chat].

signals.name: access_changed
signals.description: The player's decision for [code]social.friends.read[/code] changed to [param state]; see [method get_access]. When access ends, [signal changed] follows with an empty list.

signals.name: changed
signals.description: The friends list, or any friend's name, handle or status, changed. Emitted once per read that changed something visible.

SummerClientItems.name: SummerClientItems
SummerClientItems.brief: Read-only revisioned inventory projection for the current player.
SummerClientItems.description: Exposes the platform-owned inventory of the current authenticated player as a monotonic read-only projection. The engine owns paging and gap recovery; stale values never overwrite newer state, and no method mutates ownership, balances, or the ledger. Hosted inventory refresh requires an authenticated Player Host and the [code]player.items@1[/code] execution grant, independently of matchmaking. An explicitly launched local-emulator client with a player persona instead reads the fixture inventory frozen at initialization. That synthetic projection shares ownership identities with the local authority; it does not grant platform items or enable store and checkout services. Ordinary local clients without that fixture cannot refresh inventory. A retained facade cannot follow a new authenticated binding after shutdown/reinitialization: acquire it again from the current client. Released facades expose empty projection values and refuse new operations.

methods.name: check_refresh_readiness
methods.description: Returns the Engine's current advisory check of the same current binding and capability prerequisites used by [method refresh]. Inspect [member SummerResult.ok], [member SummerResult.code] and [member SummerResult.message]. [code]invalid_lifecycle[/code] requires initialization or rebinding after an identity change; [code]unavailable[/code] describes a missing capability or unavailable Host. No request is submitted and no provider is activated. A successful check does not guarantee later transport success or a fresh projection; the operation result remains authoritative. The base Host interface supplies inventory without a separate bootstrap capability advertisement. C# exposes [code]CheckRefreshReadiness()[/code].

methods.name: is_projection_loaded
methods.description: Whether this client binding has completed an initial inventory projection. False before the first successful refresh and after binding teardown; true for a successfully loaded empty inventory, even when [member as_of_event_sequence] is zero. Reads the SDK's existing projection state without fetching or caching anything. Loaded does not mean current or authorized: later refreshes and inventory events may change the projection, and authority still verifies equipment ownership. C# exposes [code]IsProjectionLoaded()[/code].

methods.name: get_owned_items
methods.description: Returns current items for which [method SummerInventoryItem.is_owned] is true, optionally filtered by an exact definition ID. An empty ID returns all owned items. Preserves the stable item identity order of [member items]. The returned array is independent and its item values are immutable. This reads the current inventory projection without network requests; a purchase receipt alone never grants ownership.

methods.name: has_owned_definition
methods.description: Whether the current projection contains an owned item with this exact definition ID. An empty ID returns false. Replacement and removal events are reflected immediately in subsequent queries. This is a local projection query, not authority to grant or equip an item on a server.

methods.name: refresh
methods.description: Re-reads the full projection through bounded platform pages (or the frozen explicit local fixture); completes once the projection is consistent at-or-after the sequence that triggered the refresh.

members.name: as_of_event_sequence
members.description: Monotonic projection watermark.

members.name: availability
members.description: Compatibility view of [method check_refresh_readiness]. [member SummerAvailability.hosted_sessions_available] reports inventory refresh readiness here; the local flags are false. Prefer the named readiness method for an operation-specific result and diagnostic.

members.name: items
members.description: The current read-only item projections, ordered by stable item identity.

signals.name: item_removed
signals.description: An item left the projection.

signals.name: item_replaced
signals.description: An item value was replaced at a newer revision.

signals.name: refreshed
signals.description: A refresh walk completed and the projection is consistent.

SummerClientMatchmaking.name: SummerClientMatchmaking
SummerClientMatchmaking.description: Matchmaking is one placement provider among several; entering a World goes through [method SummerClient.join] with [method SummerJoinTarget.queue]. This facade only reports whether hosted placement is available right now.

members.name: availability
members.description: Current local and hosted capability projection.

SummerClientMessages.name: SummerClientMessages
SummerClientMessages.brief: The player's Summer direct messages, behind the player's per-Game consent.

methods.name: get_access
methods.description: Returns the player's latest known decision for the messaging [param permission] in this Game: [code]granted[/code], [code]declined[/code], [code]revoked[/code], [code]not_requested[/code], or [code]undeclared[/code]. The Engine reads the decisions when the event stream starts or resyncs and after a consent decision, and every messaging operation's answer updates its own permission. An unknown permission name is [code]undeclared[/code].

methods.name: is_available
methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when the Summer app offers direct messages ([code]player.messaging@1[/code]) to this signed-in player. Always [code]false[/code] in local play, for guests, and for accounts the platform does not allow social features ([code]age_restricted[/code]). The player must still grant each permission.

methods.name: list_conversations
methods.description: Reads one page of the player's conversations. Pass [member SummerConversationsOperation.next_cursor] from the previous page as [param cursor] to continue. [param limit] is the page size, from [code]1[/code] to [code]100[/code], or [code]0[/code] for the platform default; the platform may return fewer.

methods.name: list_messages
methods.description: Reads one page of the conversation with [param user_id]. Pass [member SummerDirectMessagesOperation.next_cursor] from the previous page as [param cursor] to continue. [param limit] matches [method list_conversations].

methods.name: list_messages_after
methods.description: Reads messages in the conversation with [param user_id] whose [member SummerDirectMessage.sequence] is above [param sequence], in ascending order: the catch-up read after [signal messages_changed]. [param sequence] must be above [code]0[/code].

methods.name: mark_read
methods.description: Marks the conversation with [param user_id] read up to the message [param sequence], on every device the player uses.

methods.name: request_access
methods.description: Asks the Summer app to show its consent sheet for the messaging [param permissions]: [code]social.messages.read[/code], [code]social.messages.send[/code] and [code]social.messages.read_state.write[/code]. Only the trusted app records the player's decision; the Engine then reads it. Succeeds when the player granted every requested permission, at once when they already had; otherwise fails with the first refusal, such as [code]permission_declined[/code], or [code]permission_not_requested[/code] when the player closed the sheet without deciding. Fails at once with [code]permission_undeclared[/code] when this Build does not declare a requested permission, [code]invalid_argument[/code] for any other name, and [code]ui_unavailable[/code] when the app cannot show the sheet now. One consent sheet is requested at a time, shared with [method SummerClientFriends.request_access].

methods.name: send
methods.description: Sends [param text] to the friend [param user_id]. The text is 1 to 4000 characters, not only whitespace, with no control characters other than newline and tab; anything else fails with [code]invalid_argument[/code] before any request. On success, [member SummerDirectMessageSendOperation.message] is the accepted message. Each call is one message: the Engine never sends it twice.

signals.name: messages_changed
signals.description: The player's direct messages may have changed: a message arrived or was read on another device, or the event stream resynced and changes may have been missed. Re-read the pages the game shows. Pending native Host support: the Summer apps do not yet forward message hints to games, so today this fires only after a stream resync.

SummerClientParty.name: SummerClientParty
SummerClientParty.brief: The player's Summer party as this Game sees it.

methods.name: get_all_data
methods.description: Returns a copy of this Game's party data as [String] keys and values. Empty outside a party.

methods.name: get_data
methods.description: Returns this Game's party data for [param key], or [param default] when the key is not set.

methods.name: get_leader
methods.description: Returns the party leader, or [code]null[/code] outside a party.

methods.name: get_local_member
methods.description: Returns this player's own member entry, or [code]null[/code] outside a party.

methods.name: get_member_limit
methods.description: Returns the party's maximum size, or [code]0[/code] when it is unknown.

methods.name: get_members
methods.description: Returns the current members in join order. Each entry is an immutable [SummerPartyMember] for the current snapshot; key your UI by [member SummerPartyMember.user_id].

methods.name: get_search_queue
methods.description: Returns the queue the party is searching in this Game, or an empty [StringName] when no party search is in progress.

methods.name: is_available
methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when the Summer app offers parties to this signed-in player. Always [code]false[/code] in local play, for guests, for accounts the platform does not allow parties ([code]age_restricted[/code]), and in Summer apps without the [code]player.party@1[/code] capability.

methods.name: is_in_party
methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when the player currently belongs to a Summer party.

methods.name: is_leader
methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] when this player leads their party.

methods.name: is_searching
methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while a party search in this Game is in progress. See [method get_search_queue].

methods.name: refresh
methods.description: Reads the party snapshot again through the Player Host. Normally unnecessary: the Engine already re-reads it on every change. One read is in flight at a time; a second call while pending returns the same operation. Fails with [code]capability_unavailable[/code] when [method is_available] is [code]false[/code], [code]age_restricted[/code] when the platform refuses parties to this account, [code]unavailable[/code] (retryable) when the Player Host cannot be reached, or [code]protocol_error[/code] for a malformed snapshot, which changes nothing.

methods.name: set_data
methods.description:
Sets this Game's party data for [param key]; an empty [param value] deletes the key. Only the leader can set party data. Keys are 1 to 32 characters of [code]a-z[/code], [code]0-9[/code], [code]_[/code], [code].[/code] and [code]-[/code]; values are at most 256 UTF-8 bytes of text without control characters and pass the Summer chat text filter; a party holds at most 16 keys per Game.
The Engine refuses before any network request with [code]not_party_leader[/code] for a member, [code]party_not_found[/code] outside a party, or [code]invalid_argument[/code] for a key, value or key count outside these limits. The platform remains the authority and may still refuse with the same codes, or with [code]text_not_allowed[/code] when the text filter rejects the value. Writes are applied in call order and fenced by the party version; if the party changed underneath a write, the Engine re-reads it and sends the write once more before failing with retryable [code]party_version_conflict[/code]. On success, [signal data_changed] has already fired.

methods.name: set_member_data
methods.description: Sets this player's own member data for this Game, such as [code]ready[/code] or [code]character[/code]; an empty [param value] deletes the key. Any member can set their own data, up to 8 keys per Game. Key and value limits, ordering, version fencing and failures match [method set_data], except that it is never refused for leadership. Member data is removed when the member leaves the party.

methods.name: show_invite_dialog
methods.description: Asks the Summer app to present its friend invite sheet over the game. The app creates a party first when the player has none. The operation completes when the app's presenter answers. The Summer app answers as soon as the sheet is on screen, not when the player closes it, so the game keeps running and receives party changes while the sheet is open. It fails with [code]ui_unavailable[/code] when the app cannot present the sheet right now and nothing is shown, and with [code]capability_unavailable[/code] when [method is_available] is [code]false[/code]. Invitations sent from the sheet reach the game only as later party changes.

methods.name: show_party_dialog
methods.description: Asks the Summer app to present party management (leave, kick, leadership transfer and party chat) over the game. Completes when the app's presenter answers, as soon as the sheet is on screen; failures match [method show_invite_dialog]. One request is in flight at a time: while the app has not answered, asking for the same sheet returns the pending operation and asking for the other fails with retryable [code]operation_in_progress[/code].

signals.name: changed
signals.description: The party snapshot changed in any way this Game can see. Emitted once per change, after every more specific signal for that change.

signals.name: data_changed
signals.description: This Game's party data for [param key] was set, changed or deleted. Joining a party reports each key it already holds; leaving a party reports each key it held.

signals.name: leader_changed
signals.description: Leadership moved to [param member] inside the same party. Joining or leaving a party reports the leader through [signal member_joined] and [signal member_left] instead.

signals.name: member_data_changed
signals.description: A member who stayed in the party set, changed or deleted their data for [param key]. A joining member's data arrives with [signal member_joined].

signals.name: member_in_game_changed
signals.description: A member who stayed in the party opened or closed this Game; read [member SummerPartyMember.in_game].

signals.name: member_joined
signals.description: [param member] is now in the party. When this player joins a party, it fires for every member, including this player's own entry.

signals.name: member_left
signals.description: [param member], as last seen, is no longer in the party. When this player leaves, the snapshot becomes empty and it fires for every former member, including this player's own entry.

signals.name: search_ended
signals.description: The party search in this Game reached a terminal state, or this player left the party during it.

signals.name: search_started
signals.description: The party leader started a party search in [param queue] of this Game, or this player joined a party that is searching. A member follows with [code]Summer.client.join(SummerJoinTarget.party_queue(queue))[/code].

SummerClientPlayerData.name: SummerClientPlayerData
SummerClientPlayerData.brief: Read-only view of this player's own public player data.
SummerClientPlayerData.description: Reads the public slot the Game's hosted authority wrote for this player, for example to show a rank in the lobby before matchmaking. Clients cannot write player data, and the secret slot never reaches the client. Games without a hosted authority fail with [code]player_data_unavailable[/code].

methods.name: load
methods.description: Reads this player's public record through the trusted Player Host. [member SummerPlayerDataLoadOperation.secret_record] is always [code]null[/code].

SummerClientRankings.name: SummerClientRankings
SummerClientRankings.description: Reads a ranking declared by the active Game through the authenticated Player Host. It works in standalone games before any matchmaking Session exists. The caller can read only their own score and standing; leaderboard rows contain display names, not account IDs. Each method returns a typed operation whose result may be awaited.

methods.name: get_score
methods.description: Reads this player's current score, games and version on [param ranking]. The ranking ID uses lower-case ASCII letters, digits and single separators (period, underscore or hyphen), up to 64 characters.

methods.name: leaderboard
methods.description: Reads the top 50 rows, including players with zero games. The caller's row has [member SummerLeaderboardEntry.you] set when present.

methods.name: standing
methods.description: Reads this player's full rank and total player count. Rank is zero until the player's first score is committed.

SummerClientRatings.name: SummerClientRatings
SummerClientRatings.brief: This player's own match results and committed account ratings.
SummerClientRatings.description:
Two facts converge here and game code never has to relay either. When the authority concludes a Match, the Engine delivers this Session's outcome as a [SummerMatchResult] with a pending rating and emits [signal match_result]. When the platform commits the rating, the trusted Player Host delivers it privately to this player alone; the same result moves to committed and [signal rating_committed] fires. Stale or replayed facts never overwrite newer state, and no other player's result or rating is ever visible here.
Recovery after a missed delivery is [method refresh], a bounded read through the Player Host of the same [code]value[/code], [code]games[/code], [code]version[/code] triple. Game code never calls the platform directly.

methods.name: get_current
methods.description: The latest committed rating for [param queue], or [code]null[/code] until one is known.

methods.name: leaderboard
methods.description: Reads [param queue]'s 50 highest-rated players by display name through the Player Host; [member SummerLeaderboardEntry.you] marks the caller's own row. Only the Host's own queue can be read. One read is in flight at a time; a second call for the same queue returns the pending operation.

methods.name: refresh
methods.description: Reads the committed rating for [param queue] through the Player Host. Only a strictly newer version replaces the held one. One read is in flight at a time; a second call while pending returns the same operation. Fails typed with [code]invalid_argument[/code] for an empty queue or [code]unavailable[/code] (retryable) when the Player Host cannot be reached.

methods.name: standing
methods.description: Reads the caller's own place in [param queue] through the Player Host: their rating, how many players are rated, their percentile once rated, and their leaderboard rank when it is within the top 1000. One read is in flight at a time; a second call for the same queue returns the pending operation.

members.name: last_result
members.description: The most recent result for this player, or [code]null[/code].

members.name: results
members.description: Recent results for this player, oldest first, bounded.

signals.name: match_result
signals.description: The authority concluded a Match this player took part in. [member SummerMatchResult.rating_state] is pending or none; no rating values are present yet.

signals.name: rating_changed
signals.description: The current rating for [param queue] advanced, through a commit, a platform snapshot, or [method refresh].

signals.name: rating_committed
signals.description: The platform committed this player's rating for the Match in [param result]; [member SummerMatchResult.rating] is now set.

SummerClientStore.name: SummerClientStore
SummerClientStore.brief: Browse the current Game store and request trusted checkout.
SummerClientStore.description: Lists immutable platform items and Sparks display prices through the trusted Player Host. Browsing requires the advertised [code]player.store.read@1[/code] capability and does not require joining a multiplayer session. Checkout additionally requires [code]player.store.checkout@1[/code]. The application-owned Host displays the authoritative cart and handles approval. The Game cannot approve a purchase. A retained facade cannot follow a new authenticated binding after shutdown/reinitialization: acquire it again from the current client. Released facades expose no current checkout facts and refuse new operations.

methods.name: check_browse_readiness
methods.description: Returns the Engine's advisory check of the authenticated binding and [code]player.store.read@1[/code] prerequisites also used by [method list_items]. The [SummerResult] includes a code and diagnostic message. [code]invalid_lifecycle[/code] requires initialization or rebinding after an identity change; [code]unavailable[/code] describes a missing execution/Host capability or unavailable Host. Does not submit, activate a provider, reserve capacity or guarantee later success. Arguments, in-flight page limits and transport results remain the operation's responsibility. C# exposes [code]CheckBrowseReadiness()[/code].

methods.name: check_checkout_readiness
methods.description: Returns the Engine's advisory check of the same authenticated binding, [code]player.store.checkout@1[/code] grants and durable outcome event support used by [method request_checkout]. Readiness is independent of browsing and existing pending purchases. A known terminal outcome event-stream failure makes new checkout creation unavailable until the authenticated binding is restored. [code]invalid_lifecycle[/code] requires initialization or rebinding after an identity change; [code]unavailable[/code] describes missing prerequisites. The result includes a diagnostic message. No request, approval, acknowledgment or provider activation occurs. A successful check does not validate a cart, reserve capacity, approve a purchase or guarantee success. Recovery of existing outcomes continues independently of permission to create a new purchase. Every deliberate checkout call still creates a new identity: never retry an unknown purchase through another call. C# exposes [code]CheckCheckoutReadiness()[/code].

methods.name: has_pending_checkouts
methods.description:
Whether [method get_pending_checkout_request_ids] is nonempty. Includes requests without a quote, canceled or dropped observation handles, and recovered pending or manual-review outcomes. Terminal outcomes and definite no-effect refusals are not pending. This queries existing retained facts without submitting, polling, retrying, or acknowledging anything. False describes this binding's local knowledge, not a guarantee that durable recovery is complete.
For a checkout panel, connect [signal checkout_status_changed] synchronously, then render [method get_checkout_statuses] and query this method. Re-query after requesting checkout, on operation completion, and in each status callback instead of retaining another pending-ID or version map for rendering. Rendering should tolerate duplicate facts; side effects still require identity-based deduplication. Operation completion should display a creation failure only when no authoritative status exists and [method SummerCheckoutOperation.is_outcome_unknown] is false. Preserve canonical terminal status messages rather than overwriting them with a generic operation failure. Closing a panel disconnects observation and never cancels a purchase.

methods.name: list_items
methods.description: Requests one page containing at most [param limit] items (1 to 100). Pass the previous operation's [member SummerStoreItemsOperation.next_cursor] to request another page. An empty cursor starts browsing. Completion is deferred; inspect the operation result before reading items. A second request while one is in flight fails with [code]operation_in_progress[/code]. Cancellation discards the page and drains the old request before another may start. Game code supplies no Game ID, buyer identity, credentials, or prices.

methods.name: request_checkout
methods.description: Requests one cart containing 1 to 16 unique offers and at most 64 total units. Prices and authenticated identity come from the trusted Host. Human approval happens in application-owned UI. Creation acceptance is not purchase completion. The returned operation completes on purchased or a definite terminal failure; manual review remains unresolved. Dropping or canceling the operation does not cancel a purchase or discard the durable outcome. No status polling or Game approval API is exposed.

methods.name: get_checkout_statuses
methods.description: Returns retained checkout states for this authenticated player and Game. Connect [signal checkout_status_changed] before inspecting retained state. Enumeration does not acknowledge delivery. Unobserved terminal outcomes remain durable in the Host/backend and locally retained; new requests are refused when the bounded retention capacity is full.

methods.name: get_pending_checkout_request_ids
methods.description: Returns sorted retained unresolved request identities for this authenticated binding, including requests without a quote response and canceled or dropped handles. Terminal outcomes and definite no-effect refusals disappear from this list. Enumeration does not acknowledge or retry anything. Account changes and shutdown clear the local binding; the trusted Host recovers durable outcomes after rebinding. This list is local knowledge, not a claim that a request was accepted or that recovery is complete.

members.name: availability
members.description: Compatibility view of [method check_browse_readiness]. The existing [member SummerAvailability.hosted_sessions_available] flag reports whether browsing is available, independently of matchmaking; both local flags are false. Prefer [method check_browse_readiness] and [method check_checkout_readiness] for operation-specific results and diagnostics. The operation result remains authoritative.

signals.name: checkout_status_changed
signals.description: Delivers retained authoritative checkout state through a standard synchronous connection. Terminal delivery is acknowledged internally only after a synchronous callback returns and the authenticated binding still matches. A crash before acknowledgment may replay delivery: deduplicate by request ID and version. This guarantees callback dispatch, not successful Game business processing. Deferred-only connections do not acknowledge delivery. No listeners means the outcome is retained until a synchronous listener connects. Receipt handling never grants inventory; canonical inventory remains authoritative.

SummerExecutionContext.description: Created only by trusted native bootstrap. Lifecycle readiness is separate from local/online mode; role, topology, profile, and capabilities live in [member execution].

SummerJoinTarget.name: SummerJoinTarget
SummerJoinTarget.brief: Which placement provider brings this player into a World.
SummerJoinTarget.description:
The single argument of [method SummerClient.join]. A target is an immutable statement of intent built with one of the static constructors: [method queue] for solo matchmaking, [method party_queue] to queue with the account party, [method world] for a direct or open World join, [method invite] for a private code, [method follow] for a party or player, [method portal] for an authority-issued transfer, [method resume] for a reconnect, and [method local] for the in-process development fixture.
Every target yields the same [SummerJoinOperation], the same progress stages, the same typed failures, and the same [SummerWorld] and [SummerSession] after admission. Only queue targets can ever raise [signal SummerJoinOperation.acceptance_required]; a game that never matchmakes never sees a proposal or a Match.
Targets carry safe intent only. They never contain tickets, tokens, endpoints, or platform identifiers.

methods.name: follow
methods.description: Join the World a party or player is currently in.

methods.name: get_queue
methods.description: Queue name for a queue target, otherwise empty. Exposed as a method because the static factory [method queue] owns the [code skip-lint]queue[/code] name.

methods.name: invite
methods.description: Join through a private code or a server-browser entry.

methods.name: local
methods.description: Join a local development World over loopback. No platform is involved. [param port] [code]0[/code] selects the default local port. A sandboxed embedded Debug app must explicitly authorize its admitted package and exact preview endpoint before Engine startup; a game cannot grant this permission. Missing authorization fails with nonretryable [code]capability_unavailable[/code]. This preview does not grant hosted access or general network permission.

methods.name: party_queue
methods.description:
Enter the named queue together with the player's current Summer party. The same target serves every member. When the leader joins it, the party search starts; every member must have this Game open with a compatible Build, otherwise the join fails with retryable [code]party_member_offline[/code]. When another member joins it, they attach to the party's search in progress for the same queue and receive their own Session in the same match; with no such search it fails with retryable [code]party_not_searching[/code]. Members typically join when [signal SummerClientParty.search_started] fires. Outside a party it fails with [code]party_not_found[/code].
Every party member goes through the same search, proposal, cancellation and admission lifecycle as [method queue], and receives the ordinary join result. Party membership and private chat persist across Games and remain owned by the Summer account; the game never receives the party's private chat history or credentials. Requires a Host advertising [code]find_party_session[/code]; unavailable Hosts fail explicitly. Local play has no account party and fails with [code]capability_unavailable[/code].
[codeblock]
var party := Summer.client.party
party.search_started.connect(func(queue: StringName) -> void:
    if not party.is_leader():
        var result := await Summer.client.join(SummerJoinTarget.party_queue(queue)).completed
        if not result.is_ok():
            push_warning(result.message)
)
[/codeblock]

methods.description: Enter through matchmaking on the named queue. The optional [param request] only tunes region preferences and the bounded search lifetime; a request naming a different queue fails the join with [code]invalid_argument[/code]. When the queue declares acceptance, the operation pauses at [constant SummerJoinProgress.STAGE_PROPOSED] and emits [signal SummerJoinOperation.acceptance_required].

SummerMatchResult.name: SummerMatchResult
SummerMatchResult.brief: This player's own view of one concluded Match.

Two facts converge in one object and nothing else does. When the authority's settlement commits, the Engine delivers to exactly this Session its [member outcome], with [member rating_state] at [constant RATING_STATE_PENDING] and no rating values: the authority never relays account data. Later the platform commits this player's rating and delivers it privately through the trusted Player Host; the same object then carries [member rating] and moves to [constant RATING_STATE_COMMITTED]. Queues without a rating stay at [constant RATING_STATE_NONE].
The object is keyed by [member match_id] and [member session_id]. A rating fact for another Match or Session never touches it, and a replayed or older fact is ignored: only a strictly newer [member SummerRatingSnapshot.version] on [member SummerRatingChange.after] is applied.

SummerMatchmakingProposal.name: SummerMatchmakingProposal
SummerMatchmakingProposal.brief: Opaque handle for one pending matchmaking proposal that requires an explicit decision.
SummerMatchmakingProposal.description:
Every matchmaking proposal requires an explicit creator decision; the engine never accepts on the game's behalf. The handle arrives through [signal SummerJoinOperation.acceptance_required] and is also readable as [member SummerJoinOperation.pending_proposal] while a decision is awaited.
The handle is deliberately opaque: it exposes only safe metadata and carries no proposal identifier, version, ticket, credential, carrier, endpoint, or platform route. The private concurrency identity stays inside the trusted runtime and is fenced per proposal, so a delayed decision made for an earlier proposal can never act on a later one — it fails with [code]proposal_stale[/code] instead.
Exactly one decision is allowed. Repeating the same decision is idempotent and returns the original outcome; the opposite decision fails with [code]proposal_already_decided[/code]. After the proposal expires, is superseded, or the matchmaking operation ends, both methods fail with [code]proposal_stale[/code] without side effects. A proposal that reaches its deadline with no decision from every player ends the matchmaking operation with [code]proposal_expired[/code].
Games that want automatic behavior connect [signal SummerJoinOperation.acceptance_required] directly to [method accept].

methods.name: accept
methods.description: Submits the explicit accept decision for this proposal through the trusted Player Host. On success the parent [SummerJoinOperation] stays pending and continues into allocation and admission only after every proposed player accepted. Fails typed with [code]proposal_stale[/code] or [code]proposal_already_decided[/code]; a failed call performs no submission.

methods.name: decline
methods.description: Submits the explicit decline decision for this proposal through the trusted Player Host. The parent [SummerJoinOperation] then terminates cleanly with the typed code [code]proposal_declined[/code]; no allocation happens and a later [method SummerClient.join] starts a fresh search. Fails typed with [code]proposal_stale[/code] or [code]proposal_already_decided[/code]; a failed call performs no submission.

methods.name: is_decided
methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] once a decision was successfully submitted through this handle.

members.name: accept_by_unix_msec

SummerOperation.name: SummerOperation
SummerOperation.brief: Single-terminal asynchronous operation for the Summer runtime.
SummerOperation.description: Completes exactly once on the main thread with a [SummerResult]. Deferred operations are owned by a revocable Summer queue until terminal queue cleanup, including cancellation, so dropping the caller reference cannot strand a queued completion. Use [method get_result_or_completed_signal] when awaiting from GDScript so a synchronously published scheduling failure cannot be missed. Scene module teardown revokes queued dispatch and publishes cancellation without invoking script callbacks. Scripts may observe or cancel an engine-created operation but cannot construct or complete one.

methods.name: cancel
methods.description: Requests cancellation on the main thread. Returns [code]true[/code] only when cancellation wins while pending. The terminal result then has code [code]&"cancelled"[/code].

methods.name: get_result_or_completed_signal
methods.description: Returns the terminal [SummerResult] when already complete, or the [signal completed] signal while pending. On the main thread, [code]var result: SummerResult = await operation.get_result_or_completed_signal()[/code] is race-free even when deferred scheduling fails synchronously before the operation is returned. Do not await [signal completed] directly unless the pending state was established without a gap.

methods.name: initialize
methods.description:
Starts initialization using the trusted Game identity supplied by the Summer Host or hosted authority launch. Omit [param game_id] for a portable build. When supplied, it asserts the expected identity and never grants authorization or overrides the launch context. With no online launch or Host, an omitted ID creates a project-scoped synthetic local identity; a supplied ID preserves that explicit local namespace. Read the resolved identity with [method get_game].
A mismatch returns [code]&"game_identity_mismatch"[/code] without publishing partial context. An incomplete/refused trusted context returns [code]&"trusted_launch_unavailable"[/code] and never falls back to local play. Successful hosted authority initialization atomically publishes immutable Game, Build, and World projections without inventing a Player or Session.
Concurrent callers that omit the ID or assert the same resolved ID share one pending operation. Ready replay preserves the current context. A conflicting in-flight or ready ID returns [code]&"identity_conflict"[/code]. Successful completion publishes [constant STATE_READY]. Cancellation restores the stable lifecycle state that preceded this initialization attempt.

Invalidation clears that window immediately and reloads the newest two. History is best effort, not a lossless event log. Keep UI text synchronized with [signal history_changed] and treat text as plain text, not markup. A receipt proves acceptance, not incoming delivery.

methods.name: refresh
methods.description: Reads the newest authorized page. Only one history read may be pending. Use this after [signal history_failed] to request recovery.

methods.name: load_older
methods.description: Reads the next older page at the current revision, up to the sixteen-message window bound. Older history never emits an incoming-message burst. Fails when no older cursor exists, a read is pending, the window is full, or history is dirty.

methods.name: close

Messages are ordered within each newest-page batch; visibility changes may expose previously unseen older messages in a later batch. Delivery is deduplicated within a bounded local history; it is not exactly once across lifetimes.

signals.name: closed

SummerWorldLoadOperation.name: SummerWorldLoadOperation
SummerWorldLoadOperation.brief: Loads the current World save through its trusted owner.
SummerWorldLoadOperation.description: A successful result exposes a validated save, including schema and Build identity. Failure preserves admission closure. This operation does not deserialize or run game code.

methods.name: get_save
methods.description: The immutable load result after success; null before completion or on failure.

SummerWorldSave.name: SummerWorldSave
SummerWorldSave.brief: A validated saved World or explicit pristine World.
SummerWorldSave.description: Opaque game-defined bytes. Apply and validate these bytes before acknowledging restoration. A pristine World has revision zero and no digest; a failed load never returns a pristine World.

methods.name: has_save
methods.description: Whether a previously committed save exists.

methods.name: get_data
methods.description: Returns game-defined bytes. Mutating the returned array cannot change this load result.

SummerWorldSaveOperation.name: SummerWorldSaveOperation
SummerWorldSaveOperation.description: Retries preserve the exact save identity and bytes. A timeout may leave an unknown commit outcome; retry the original request to recover its receipt. An expected revision prevents overwriting newer state.

methods.name: get_receipt
methods.description: The durable receipt after successful completion; null otherwise.

SummerWorldSaveReceipt.name: SummerWorldSaveReceipt
SummerWorldSaveReceipt.description: Returned by a successful World save commit. Receipt identity belongs to one World runtime. A successful upload alone is not a receipt. Cancellation or timeout cannot prove that a save was not committed.

methods.name: get_revision
methods.description: Canonical positive decimal revision.

methods.name: get_save_id
methods.description: Creator supplied save identity, retained across retries.

methods.name: get_schema
methods.description: Published game save schema.

methods.name: get_sha256
methods.description: SHA-256 digest of the exact game bytes.

methods.name: get_state_sequence
methods.description: Game supplied capture watermark as a canonical decimal string.

methods.name: get_build_id
methods.description: Build recorded with this revision, as provenance. A World's long-running state is not tied to a Build: a save written by an earlier Build restores whenever its schema matches.

methods.name: get_bytes
methods.description: Decoded save size in bytes.
